connector: Last time, Jemmy took his whacks without a sound, and the prince went back on his word. Today the prince sneaks into Jemmy’s room at night with a plan. Read to find out what he wants, and why Jemmy has to go along.

plate.look: A forest clearing on a foggy morning, painted by Arkhip Kuindzhi more than 100 years ago. In Chapter 4, a thick fog swirls in and the boys lose the road.

a.raw: i am not afraid of you jemmy said to billy
a.fixed: “I am not afraid of you,” Jemmy said to Billy.
a.why: Quotation marks go around Jemmy’s exact words. I is always a capital. A comma goes inside the closing quotation mark. Jemmy and Billy are names, so they get capitals. A period ends the sentence.

b.raw: stay close to me jemmy said to the prince
b.fixed: “Stay close to me,” Jemmy said to the prince.
b.why: Quotation marks go around Jemmy’s exact words, and Stay starts them with a capital. A comma goes inside the closing quotation mark. Jemmy is a name, so it gets a capital. A period ends the sentence.

match.astonishment: Astonishment is a feeling, a really big one. Look for the meaning about great surprise.
match.gallows: Gallows is a thing, not a feeling. Look for the meaning about a frame.
match.strayed: Strayed is something you do with your feet when you get lost. Look for the meaning about wandering off.
match.cutthroat: A cutthroat is a kind of person, and not a nice one. Look for the meaning about a dangerous criminal.

scholar.journal-q1: … and tell why the sewers would be a good place for Jemmy to hide.
scholar.journal-q2: … and explain what Jemmy is afraid they will do.
scholar.journal-q3: … and tell what this shows about the prince.

wordgame.title: Up the North Tower
wordgame.sub: Jemmy’s little room is at the top. Every right answer lights a step.
wordgame.look: This is the north tower of the castle, where Jemmy sleeps. Tiny stairs zig-zag up the stone wall. You light 8 steps each day this week. On Day 4 you reach Jemmy’s window at the top.
wordgame.todo: Read the question. Tap the answer you think is right. A right answer lights the next step.
wordgame.win: Today’s 8 steps are lit. Come back next lesson to climb higher.
wordgame.winWeek: You reached Jemmy’s window at the top of the north tower!

items.title: Pick the joining word
items.q: Jemmy was tired, ___ he still got out of bed.
items.why: but: being tired and getting up anyway push against each other.

miss.0: and just adds an idea. These two halves push against each other.
miss.2: so shows a result. Did being tired make him get up?

items.title: Pick the joining word
items.q: The prince was bored, ___ he decided to run away.
items.why: so: being bored is the reason he runs away.

miss.0: and just adds an idea. Here one half causes the other.
miss.1: but shows a difference. Does running away go against being bored?

items.title: Pick the joining word
items.q: The fog was thick, ___ the trees closed in.
items.why: and: both halves add more trouble.

miss.1: but shows a difference. Both halves here are bad news.
miss.2: so shows a result. The fog didn’t make the trees move.

items.title: Pick the joining word
items.q: The prince wore a black cloak, ___ he carried a big basket.
items.why: and: it adds one more thing he had.

miss.1: but shows a difference. Nothing here pushes against anything.
miss.2: so shows a result. The cloak didn’t cause the basket.

items.title: Pick the joining word
items.q: Jemmy wanted to slip away, ___ a lantern glowed in the fog.
items.why: but: the lantern gets in the way of his plan.

miss.0: and just adds an idea. The lantern ruins his plan.
miss.2: so shows a result. Wanting to slip away didn’t make the lantern appear.

items.title: Pick the joining word
items.q: They were lost in the forest, ___ Jemmy got down to lead the horse.
items.why: so: being lost is why Jemmy has to lead the horse.

miss.0: and just adds an idea. Here one half is the reason for the other.
miss.1: but shows a difference. Leading the horse makes sense when you’re lost.

items.title: Pick the joining word
items.q: It was night, ___ the moon was bright.
items.why: but: night is dark, yet the moon made it bright.

miss.0: and just adds. Dark night and a bright moon push against each other.
miss.2: so shows a result. The night didn’t make the moon bright.

items.title: Think it through
items.why: so shows a result: this happened, so that happened.

glossary.m: a boy kept in the castle to be punished whenever the prince does something wrong
a joining word, like and, but, or so
two vowels side by side that make one sound, like ai in rain
one beat in a word. Rain-bow has two.
what you think, said in one clear sentence

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it’s Opti. Last time you met a prince who never gets punished and a boy who always does. Today the prince has a big idea, and it isn’t a good one. As you read, ask yourself: is being bored a good enough reason to drag someone else into danger? Then you’ll give your opinion a reason to stand on.
transcripts.guide1: Word work first. Today you’ll match some long words to what they mean, and you’ll go hunting for joining words inside sentences. A joining word never comes alone. It brings a whole chunk of the sentence along with it. See if you can catch the word and its chunk together.
transcripts.guide2: Before you read: the castle is about to disappear behind you. Chapter 3 happens at night, and Chapter 4 happens in a thick fog. Watch Jemmy closely. He’s thinking hard the whole time, even when he’s quiet. And keep an eye out for a glowing light.
transcripts.guide3: Yesterday you wrote a claim. Today you give it a reason, the because behind your opinion. A strong reason comes from something a character really did, not just how you feel. Look back at today’s chapters and pick the one moment that proves your point best.

notes.wordParts: inter- means “between” (interrupt, interact, international). sub- means “under” (submarine).
notes.grammar: A conjunction is a joining word. and adds an idea, but shows a difference, and so shows a result.
notes.spelling: A vowel team is two vowels that make one sound, like ai in rain. A team stays together in one syllable: rain·bow, sea·son.
notes.wgrd: Good readers notice when a character makes a bad choice, and they ask who is responsible for what happens next.
vocab: a feeling of great surprise or shock
a frame used for hanging; Jemmy fears this punishment
wandered off the path by mistake
a dangerous criminal who would do anything for money

mods.todo: Listen to Opti. Then tap the lens you will use today.
mods.script: [warmly] Here's today's reading tip. Good readers notice when a character makes a bad choice, and then watch what that choice causes. Today the prince decides to run away, and Jemmy has to go with him. As you read, ask yourself: whose idea was this, and whose fault is the trouble that follows? Then tap one of the two lenses below, and use it while you read. You don't need to write anything.

mods.todo: Tap the yellow parts. Then pick Sentence A or B and type it the right way.
mods.script: Let's fix a sentence. Look at the correct one first. The prince is talking, so his words go inside quotation marks. A comma goes before the closing quotation mark, because the sentence keeps going: the prince announced to Jemmy. Tap the yellow parts to see each rule. Then pick Sentence A or Sentence B. Add the quotation marks, the comma, and the capital letters, and type it the right way.

mods.todo: Read the three haiku out loud. Clap the beats in the first one: 5, then 7, then 5.
mods.script: This is a haiku, a tiny poem with a fixed shape. The first line has five beats, the second has seven, and the last has five again. A haiku holds one picture and doesn't explain it. Read all three out loud. Then go back to the first one and clap each beat. Snow, on, the, court, yard. That's five! Keep clapping, and check that you get five, seven, five.

mods.todo: Tap a word, then tap what it means. Match all four words.
mods.script: You already know two word parts. Inter means between, like the internet connecting computers. Sub means under, like a subway under the city. When you see a long word, find the part at the start first, then read the rest. Tap a word in the game, then tap what it means. If you're stuck, look at the first part of the word. It gives you a big clue.

mods.todo: Listen to each card. Guess the meaning, then flip the card. Then play the matching game.
mods.script: Let's be word detectives again. Here's astonishment. Read the sentence: Jemmy stared at him with dreadful astonishment. Jemmy just heard something he never expected. Now look at the parts. Astonish means to surprise, and ment turns it into a thing. So astonishment is a feeling of great surprise. Now tap Opti reads it on each card, guess the meaning, and flip the card to check. Then play the matching game.

mods.todo: Tap the joining word, then the part after it. Then write one sentence with a new joining word.
mods.script: Joining words are back, and today you're a joining-word spotter. Remember: and adds an idea, but shows a difference, and so shows what happens next. In each sentence, first tap the joining word. Then tap the part of the sentence that comes after it. That part is the new idea the joining word brings in. Last, pick one sentence and write it again with a different joining word. Notice how the meaning changes.

mods.todo: Tap every word in the two sentences that has a vowel team.
mods.script: Let's go hunting for vowel teams. A vowel team is two vowels side by side that make one sound, like the o and a in coach, or the e and a in feast. The team always stays together. Read the two sentences slowly. Every time you see two vowels working together, tap that word. There's more than one, so keep looking until the game says you found them all.

Here's something to think about. The prince runs away for one reason: he's bored. Jemmy doesn't get a choice. He has to come along and carry the basket. But out in the fog, there are no guards and no castle walls. Watch Jemmy closely. He may see a chance of his own. Who do you think is really in charge out there?

mods.todo: Read the two questions. Then read Ch. 3–4 in your book.
mods.script: Time to read Chapters 3 and 4 in your book. First, read the two Pause and Think questions below, so you know where to stop. In Chapter 3, look for the prince's real reason for running away. In Chapter 4, a thick fog rolls in and two strangers appear. Ask yourself who Jemmy thinks they are, and why he's so scared. Stop at each question, think of your answer, and keep reading.

mods.todo: Pick Explorer or Scholar. Answer the three questions in full sentences.
mods.script: Now show what you understood. Remember, a good answer is a full sentence with a detail from the book. One, what is Jemmy's plan to escape in the fog, and what stops it? Two, when the strangers grab the boys, what does Jemmy think they are, and why is he scared? Three, why does the prince pick Jemmy to run away with? Use a detail from Chapter 3. Want a challenge? Pick Scholar, and add one more detail to each answer.

mods.todo: Copy your claim from Day 1. Write one reason under it.
mods.script: On Day 1 you wrote a claim. Today you'll give it a reason. A reason tells why your claim is true. Listen to Clara. Her claim was, Prince Brat is the most unfair character. Then she added, One reason is that Prince Brat wants Jemmy whipped hard for things the prince did. See how the reason backs up the claim? Copy your claim from Day 1 into the box. Then write one reason under it. You can start with, One reason is that.

cards.astonishment: Astonishment. Jemmy stared at him with dreadful astonishment. Astonishment means a feeling of great surprise or shock.
cards.gallows: Gallows. More likely I'll be hung from the gallows. A gallows is a wooden frame that was used long ago to punish people by hanging. Jemmy is afraid of a terrible punishment.
cards.strayed: Strayed. A thick fog had swirled in, they'd strayed from the road, and trees had closed in on them. Strayed means wandered off the path by mistake.
cards.cutthroat: Cutthroat. A cutthroat! he thought. A cutthroat is a dangerous criminal who would do anything for money.

virtue.name: courage
virtue.title: Courage Watch: Did they show courage?

items.t: The prince runs away from the castle because he is bored.
items.why: Being bored is not a brave reason to run away.

items.t: In the dark, foggy forest, Jemmy starts to slip away on his own.
items.why: Going off alone into a scary forest takes courage.

items.t: The prince tells Jemmy to get down and lead the horse through the fog.
items.why: Giving orders is not brave. Jemmy is the one walking into the fog.
